desk.headline: HEPS up 11.1% to 689.87c and revenue up 11.7% to R22.7bn, helped by fuel gains; total dividend up 28.6% to 270c; tougher year ahead for farmers

other.label: PEG profit before tax
other.change: -69% after R217m of impairments; +49.9% excluding them

results: HEPS rose 11.1% to 689.87c and revenue grew 11.7% to R22.7bn, lifted by higher fuel prices and volumes.
Recurring HEPS rose 12.9% to 705.28c, but only 6.6% after stripping out once-off fuel-price gains and the sold Agriplas business.
Agrimark retail revenue rose 9.3% and its profit grew 8% excluding a property sale; PEG fuel sites took R217m of impairments, mostly on 15 weak sites.
KAL sold its Agriplas and Tego plastics businesses and bought out a minority holder in PEG.
Debt to equity fell to 29.0% from 38.1%, and the total dividend rose 28.6% to 270c.

guidance.summary: No earnings targets. KAL expects a stronger festive season but warns of lower wheat yields, higher input costs, El Nino and dry-weather risks, AGOA loss for citrus growers and pressure on consumers; capex should be about the same as FY2026 or slightly higher.

points: CEO Johann le Roux described a year of two very different halves, with a sharp slowdown in the second half.
He said fuel-price gains helped, while squeezed consumers and a weaker farm sector hurt in ways that are hard to measure.
Le Roux said KAL prefers better returns over growth that does not reward the capital invested.
Management expects little impact from losing AGOA trade benefits, as few customers rely heavily on US exports.
The finance director said return on invested capital rose to 14.8%, above the cost of capital.
call.source: The National (25 Nov 2026), Daily Dispatch (26 Nov 2026) and Investing.com (results presentation) coverage

watch: Whether fuel volumes hold up if prices stay high.
Harvests and farmer finances under El Nino, low wheat yields and higher input costs.
Whether the weak PEG sites that were impaired improve.
